title: No horn players in Covington; Petit's band as celebrities
summary: Rene was the only pianist in town and there were no horn players, so visiting jazz bands were worshipped.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: Yeah, of course there were quite a few musicians around coming.
He wasn't, he was no musician. He was, he was a honky-ton piano player.
Yeah, but I mean they had guys that could play over there anyway.
No, no, there wasn't nobody. I was the only one in the town that played.
Yes, and I, they were high for the party.
Yeah, but they had other people around, didn't they, some time to time?

No horn players, no, no. That's why when Buddy P.T. came to town, they got, you know, they were considered like, you know, celebrities, you know, after all coming to town. With jazz, you know, music like that, you know, those fellas were supposed to be, boy they were really worshipped, especially coming to the station to play. And everybody in town would come down to the station, just to get and play. It was, it was a scene. It's like TV, it's greater than TV is today for them at that time.
